title: Define compact form affordances and error-priority guidelines
creator: Avery Chen
description: Problem: Multiple teams have shipped small variations of help text, error states, and clearing affordances for compact/dense form modes. This causes inconsistent UX in Console forms (eg. token fields, multi-select chips, toggles inside compact rows) and creates a support burden for engineers to implement one-off spacing and color tokens. Goal: Provide a single, implementable guideline that defines (1) how inline help, helper affordances, and validation messages are prioritized and visually presented in compact vs default density, (2) token mappings for border/fill/text/focus/error colors across themes, and (3) clear developer patterns (HTML structure, aria attributes, and keyboard interactions) so engineers can re-use components with consistent accessibility and performance characteristics.
acceptance_criteria: Published guideline doc in Confluence that designers & frontend engineers can reference.
Figma component variants for TextField, Select, Toggle, and MultiSelectChip covering Default/Compact and Normal/Warning/Error states.
Token mapping table (token names + hex) with contrast checks against background for light/dark themes and included in the design tokens PR.
A reference implementation PR in the design system repo that updates TextField and MultiSelect components to follow the new patterns and passes unit/axe accessibility checks.
QA checklist with keyboard and screenreader verification steps added to the ticket.
design_decisions: Hierarchy: Error messages take precedence over helper text; when space is constrained (compact), helper text should collapse to an icon-only affordance that opens a tooltip/popover.
Inline vs Summary: If multiple field-level errors exist, show the most severe inline error; surface a form-level error summary at the top with links to individual fields.

Token strategy: Introduce tokens 'form.border.compact', 'form.fill.compact', 'form.text.helper.compact', 'form.focus.ring.compact' to capture compact variants and keep existing tokens for default density.
Validation semantics: Distinguish severity levels (info, warning, error) and map to tokens 'status.info', 'status.warning', 'status.error' — engineers must render only one severity per field.
Accessibility: All validation messages must be linked via aria-describedby and focus should be moved to the first invalid form control on submit.
